Link to zuregex from C

Source: vignettes/articles/c-api.Rmd
c-api.Rmd

This guide is for the author of an R package whose C or C++ code needs regular expressions. It shows how to depend on zuregex in place of bundling PCRE2, and how to compile, match, read groups and substitute with the zr_*() functions. It assumes you have written .Call code before.

Declare the dependency

The package needs zuregex twice in DESCRIPTION: LinkingTo provides the headers, and Imports loads zuregex, which is what registers its functions.

Imports: zuregex
LinkingTo: zuregex

Imports alone does not load zuregex before your code runs. NAMESPACE needs a real import as well, of any function:

importFrom(zuregex, zuregex_info)

Nothing is added to src/Makevars. The functions are found when the package is loaded, not when it is linked, so your package holds no copy of PCRE2.

Compile and match

Include <zuregex-r.h>. A pattern is a zr_pattern, and the offsets of a match go into a zr_match_data made for that pattern. zr_match() returns a positive number when it finds a match, and ZR_NOMATCH when it does not. This .Call routine returns whether a string matches a pattern.

#include <string.h>
#include <R.h>
#include <Rinternals.h>
#include <zuregex-r.h>

SEXP has_match(SEXP pattern, SEXP x) {
  const char *pat = Rf_translateCharUTF8(STRING_ELT(pattern, 0));
  const char *s = Rf_translateCharUTF8(STRING_ELT(x, 0));

  char err[256];
  zr_pattern *p = zr_compile(pat, strlen(pat), 0, ZR_DIALECT_PCRE,
                             err, sizeof(err));
  if (p == NULL) Rf_error("%s", err);

  zr_match_data *md = zr_match_data_create(p);
  int rc = zr_match(p, s, strlen(s), 0, 0, md);

  zr_match_data_free(md);
  zr_free(p);
  return Rf_ScalarLogical(rc > 0);
}

The third argument of zr_compile() takes the flags of re_compile() in bit form, such as ZR_CASELESS for i. When compiling fails, it returns NULL and writes a message into err.

Read the groups

After a match, zr_offsets() gives where a group starts and ends. Group 0 is the whole match, and zr_group_number() turns a name into a number.

size_t start, end;
if (zr_offsets(md, 1, &start, &end) == ZR_OK) {
  /* group 1 is the bytes s[start] to s[end - 1] */
}

The offsets are not the ones the R functions return. In C they are zero-based, half-open and in bytes; re_locate() gives one-based, inclusive offsets in characters. Convert when a result goes back to R.

Substitute

zr_substitute() writes the subject with its matches replaced into a buffer you supply. size holds the size of the buffer going in and the length of the result coming out. If the buffer is too small, the call returns ZR_ERROR_NOMEMORY and sets size to what it needs, so try again with that.

size_t size = 256;
char *out = R_alloc(size, 1);
int rc = zr_substitute(p, s, strlen(s), tmpl, strlen(tmpl),
                       ZR_SUBSTITUTE_GLOBAL, NULL, out, &size);
if (rc == ZR_ERROR_NOMEMORY) {
  out = R_alloc(size, 1);
  rc = zr_substitute(p, s, strlen(s), tmpl, strlen(tmpl),
                     ZR_SUBSTITUTE_GLOBAL, NULL, out, &size);
}
if (rc < 0) Rf_error("%s", zr_strerror(rc));

The template has the syntax of re_replace(). Without ZR_SUBSTITUTE_GLOBAL only the first match is replaced.

Limits and threads

zr_set_limits(md, match, depth, heap) bounds every match run with that match data, as re_limits() does in R; a search that hits one returns ZR_ERROR_MATCH_LIMIT, ZR_ERROR_DEPTH_LIMIT or ZR_ERROR_HEAP_LIMIT.

No zr_*() function raises an R error or allocates an R object, so they can run on worker threads under two rules. A compiled pattern may be shared between threads, but each thread needs its own zr_match_data. And in each C file that calls zr_*() from a worker thread, call zuregex_api() once on the main thread first, since the first call looks the functions up through R.

What stays stable

Patterns and match data are opaque handles, and the headers name no PCRE2 type. An upgrade of the PCRE2 inside zuregex therefore never changes your build. The function table is versioned and only grows: a package built against an older zuregex keeps working with a newer one.

See also

The two headers are the reference for the C API: zuregex.h has every flag, option and status code, and zuregex-r.h the zr_*() functions. For limits on the R side, read Bound the work of a match.
